evidence.note: Downloaded the three vendored libs, then explicitly renamed to flat paths and verified SHA256 hashes — shows it harvested the pinned-hash + not-under-js/ trap early, a hard constraint most miss.

Built a broad, correctly-decomposed subsystem set (auth, serializers, timelines, admin, sse) plus templates for visibility icons, threads, error pages — reflecting a wide and accurate mental model of the Mastodon API/UI shape.

Tests targeting idempotent posting, OAuth+PKCE, RFC7662 introspection, visibility icons, local/federated split, and admin scopes confirm it extracted these specific spec constraints, not just headline features.
Probed response headers/CSP and verified seeded-status counts/authors — evidence of capturing security-header and seed-minima constraints.

No WebFetch or any consultation of docs.joinmastodon.org and no visible explicit categorized constraint inventory; API shapes appear driven by internal knowledge rather than the deferred wire contract.

reasoning: Behaviorally the agent went well beyond anchor 5: it captured not just the obvious hard constraints (health endpoint, start.sh, pinned libs, OAuth) but also subtle ones — flat-path hash verification, idempotency, RFC7662 introspection, admin scopes, visibility icons, CSP headers, and seed minima — spanning most anchor-8 categories. But it shows no consultation of the actual Mastodon wire contract and no visible systematic/categorized inventory, which are core to the anchor-8 'grounds API shapes in the real contract' half. That places it above 5 but short of 8, at a 6.
